Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-circumscribed, lobulated mass in the right lower lung zone (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of a primary lung carcinoma such as adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma. While breast tissue can overlap this region, the distinct lobulated morphology and intrapulmonary location strongly favor a primary lung malignancy over breast pathology or metastasis.
